idea: Generate a long-only moving-average crossover backtest using daily Open and Close prices. Buy when the 5-day SMA crosses above the 20-day SMA; sell when it crosses below. Detect signals at the close and execute at the next bar's open.
expected_explanation: Describe both entry and exit conditions, and distinguish the signal bar from the next bar where the trade fills.
State that trade logs and return calculations use the same execution timestamps and prices, including the same fee and slippage assumptions.
expected_code: Compute crossover signals from closing prices without using future data to decide the signal.
Record entries and exits at the next bar's timestamp and Open price, rather than the crossover bar's Close price.
Calculate position exposure and returns consistently with those fill prices. A simple shifted-position close-to-close calculation must not be presented as equivalent to next-open fills.

Using deterministic sample prices, P&L derived from logged fills must reconcile with the corresponding strategy equity change under the stated assumptions, accounting separately for any open position.
Do not record an executed trade for a last-bar signal when no following bar exists.
Provide one coherent backtest implementation without placeholder trade logic or discarded backtest loops.
Wait for complete moving-average windows before comparing indicators; do not compare partially warmed averages.
Calculate closed-trade summary statistics using valid boolean masks on realized P&L, and handle empty win/loss groups without errors.

idea: Generate a moving-average crossover backtest that rejects invalid window sizes with clear errors. Cover fast=0, slow=20; fast=-5, slow=20; fast=5, slow=0; and fast=5, slow=-20. Also reject a slow window smaller than the fast window.
expected_explanation: State that both windows must be positive integers and that slow must be greater than or equal to fast.
Explain that invalid window sizes are rejected rather than silently changed or used to calculate indicators.
expected_code: Validate fast and slow independently before calling rolling calculations; checking only slow < fast is insufficient.
Raise a clear ValueError for every listed zero or negative window case, identifying the invalid parameter.
Reject noninteger windows and slow < fast; retain support for valid positive windows such as fast=5, slow=20.

idea: Generate a long-only 5-day/20-day moving-average crossover backtest using daily Open and Close prices and a supported positive integer qty. Include examples with qty=2. Wait for complete moving-average windows, detect signals at the close, and fill only at the next bar's Open. Cover both a completed trade and a buy that fills with no later sell before the data ends: leave that position open and include the unfinished trade in the trade log. A signal on the last bar must remain unfilled because there is no next Open; never fall back to that bar's Close. Calculate realized and unrealized P&L and fractional returns correctly for qty > 1. Show hand-checked examples: entry=100, exit=110, qty=2 gives P&L=20 and return=0.10; entry=100, final Close=105, qty=2 gives unrealized P&L=10 and unrealized return=0.05. Summary formulas must remain correct for any supported quantity.
expected_explanation: Explain that the position remains open at the end of the data and has no realized exit or realized trade return.
Distinguish any unrealized mark-to-market P&L included in final equity from realized P&L on completed trades.
Explain that quantity scales currency P&L but leaves the fractional return unchanged for the same price move; identify the capital denominator for any portfolio-summary return.
expected_code: Retain the actual entry timestamp and fill price, and record the unfinished trade exactly once.
Use None for exit_time, exit_price, and realized trade return; do not invent a closing fill at the last observed price.
Keep the position open through the final available bar. If equity includes unrealized P&L, calculate and label it separately from realized trade results.
Use the same entry execution convention in the open-trade log and in the strategy return calculation.
Leave final-bar signals unfilled; never use a last-bar Close fallback for either an entry or an exit.
Wait for the full 5-day and 20-day windows before comparing averages; do not use min_periods=1 to compare averages built from different amounts of history.
For closed trades, compute realized P&L = (exit_price - entry_price) * qty and realized return = realized P&L / (entry_price * qty), with valid positive denominators.
For open trades, compute unrealized P&L = (final_close - entry_price) * qty and unrealized return = unrealized P&L / (entry_price * qty); keep realized fields None.

Verify the non-unit examples in the idea: qty=2 gives realized P&L 20 and return 0.10 for 100 to 110, and unrealized P&L 10 and return 0.05 for 100 to 105. For qty=1, those P&L values halve while fractional returns stay unchanged.
Aggregate summary P&L from the trade records and use a documented, quantity-consistent denominator for any reported summary return.
